notes:
Five real rungs out of seven bullets. Bullet 2 is framing for bullet 3 ('examine at most two of the targetable locations'), and the page's own three Watergrass locations are candidates, not a sequence: you examine one, report, and if High Bear was asking about a different pond you go to another. That is an unordered set of three, so they share a group and all three draw at once -- a strict ladder would mark (E-5) and nothing else until the player happened to walk there. Each pond is its own step because each has its own grid, and one step has one zone and one grid.

Nothing here is observable. The three observations per pond are log messages and a dialogue choice; no key item, no item, no count. So every step carries evidence null, which is the honest answer -- the ladder positions the player, it cannot track them.

Two waits, neither a step. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 is a START gate (the next Vana'dielian day after Aqua Pura), and bullet 7 is the reward landing at 00:00 rather than an action; both are recorded as notes and flagged time_gated. The trailing 'Zoning is not required to repeat this quest' is a cooldown remark. Fame 'avun' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so region is null and the raw is kept. The wiki form 'High Bear (A)' is written as-is; the normaliser folds it to the in-game 'High Bear'.

ADVERSARY (stage D): downgraded to medium. Bullet 2 says "examine at most two of the targetable locations" and bullet 5 has you visit a second pond only if High Bear was describing a different one, so the player performs one pond or two -- never three. The three pond steps are nevertheless recorded with optional false, which asserts all three are required and contradicts this quest's own note. The group is kept because all-draw-at-once is the right marker behaviour for "go to whichever pond" and every step here carries evidence null, so nothing auto-advances and nothing stalls -- but the one-of-three branch is not expressible in the schema and a human should see it. Everything else on this quest survived: names, zones, grids, order and the no-evidence reading all check out against the page.

notes:
The best-evidenced quest in this batch: bullet 3's four errands each hand over their own key item, so three of them carry real evidence and the ladder can actually follow the player. They are four separate zones with no order given, so they share a group and draw at once.

Javolio is the page's own 'Optional:', and he is the one errand whose key item is deliberately NOT used as evidence -- a player who skips him must still be able to reach the hand-in, and evidence on a step nobody has to do is a stall waiting to happen. Same reasoning, smaller, at the Scouts' Coalition: the two ???s sit next to each other and are one step, but only the Record of the 17th Assembly is evidence, because the page says outright that Copy of "Adoulin's Patroness" may not be needed (and bullet 4 has you tell Roskin it is unimportant).

Step 7 is the payoff for all of it -- the three documents Roskin actually wants are its items, so holding them reads as ready-to-hand-in. Bullet 5 is an outcome, not a step. Bullet 6 is a real second visit after one game day, so it is its own rung on the same NPC. Two interaction verbs are inferred rather than stated: 'return to Roskin with a Frontier Soda' and 'use a Pickaxe on it' are both modelled as trades, which is how Adoulin handles both, and both are noted. Quest Reqs lists the Frontier Soda and Pickaxe -- they are step items, not a gate the schema has a slot for. Adoulin is not one of the nine fame regions, so region is null and the raw kept.

notes:
Twelve bullets, six of them steps. Bullets 6 to 10 are fishing advice (which rod, which bait, what the reel-in message looks like) and bullets 11 and 12 sit under 'Notes' -- a RoE cross-reference and a remark about when fame is paid. None is a rung, and a verb-scanner would have made five out of them.

Bullet 2 says there are three tasks and its sub-bullet says you need not return between them, so all six task steps share one group and draw at once. Within each task the coalition NPC comes before the field work, but between tasks there is no order at all, and a strict ladder would have pinned the player to Corpo-Vorpo.

The page never says which half of Adoulin the Peacekeepers', Pioneers' and Couriers' Coalitions are in -- only Audibert's Scouts' Coalition is placed, by the header. Those three steps therefore carry zone null rather than a guess; all three names resolve unambiguously, so the markers survive the missing zone. (A sibling page in this batch puts the Pioneers' Coalition in Western Adoulin, but that is not this page's text and is not carried across.)

Only the fishing step is observable: the Rusted pickaxe is a key item, so it is the one piece of evidence in the quest. Its requirement is 'a fishing rod and lure' with four rods and one bait named as suggestions -- no expressible AND-list, so items stays empty and items_partial is set. Item Reqs restates the same thing. The Daunting Emanation is night-only (20:00-4:00), which nothing in the packets reports.

notes:
Eleven bullets and three rungs. Bullets 3 to 11 are one battle: waves of crew, Swiftwinged Gekko arriving and fleeing, Watch Imps, temporary items handed out mid-fight, then the treasure. They are the shape of the fight, not nine things the player does, and splitting them would put eight unmarkable rungs inside a 30 minute battlefield.

The quest ends where the fight ends -- the treasure spawns, you loot it and leave by the Lifeboat Ramp. There is no hand-in, and pointing the last marker back at Halshaob would be an invention, so the ladder simply stops on the fight (cf. Operation Teatime).

The destination is recorded as the Cutter, which is what bullet 2 tells you to find and which resolves as a real entity; the Lifeboat Ramp, also real, is only ever named as the way in and out, so it is a note. Mobs: Swiftwinged Gekko is verbatim, but the page only ever writes 'Watch Imps' plural and 'the Ashu Talif's crew' / 'Crew Members' generically -- the imps are recorded singular so the live matcher has a chance, and the crew is not recorded at all because the page never gives them a name. Killing Gekko is worth a second box but is not required, so he is a mob on the fight step, not a step of his own.

Quest Reqs carries the real prerequisite -- Aht Urhgan Mission 18 -- while the Previous field is empty; it is recorded as a prev entry and flagged, since that is where a mission gate belongs. Fame 'Treasures of Aht Urhgan' is the Aht Urhgan region under its expansion name and resolves as such. The 24 hour repeat limit is a cooldown, not a rung.

You board -- and later leave -- by the Lifeboat Ramp.

30 minute limit. Waves of crew (~600 HP each, but they pile up), then Gekko, who runs for the top deck and vanishes after casting Bindga/Graviga/Paralyga/Sleepga -- he can be stunned, and killing him spawns a second box. Then Watch Imps, whose Ancient Magic reaches anywhere on the ship for 550+. Everyone is handed temporary items mid-fight; Gekko returns between waves and appears once more with the last wave, which is the final chance at him. The treasure spawns when everything is dead. The page writes 'Watch Imps' plural and never names the crew members at all.

notes:
The Scholar unlock. Four rungs, and the interesting decisions are all about gates and about the Vellum.

GATES. The header's Level is empty but bullet 1 says 'as a level 30+ job' -- any job -- so that is a level gate of 30 with jobs left empty. Bullet 4 is the trap: BLM, RDM, SMN or BLU is needed only to fire an SP ability at the very end, and the page says outright you may switch to one then and it need not be level 30. Writing those four into gates.jobs would lock the whole quest to four jobs forever, so it stays a note on step 4 and a flag.

VELLUM. Bullet 3 is a genuine step, not commentary -- Tucker is a real markable NPC and the only in-game source. It is optional because the Auction House sells Vellum under Leathercraft and that route cannot be expressed as items, which is also why items_partial is set. Either way the player ends up holding twelve sheets, so Vellum x12 is safe evidence on that step and the mark moves to Erlene the moment it is true. The trade is granular: four stacks per trade, three trades, and a short trade still burns one of the three -- 12 stacks of 12 rolanberries is what you should arrive with, so 144 is what the step asks you to hold.

Steps 3 and 4 are both Erlene and both real: the page really does wedge an action between them (use Astral Flow, Chainspell, Azure Lore or Manafont, then speak again). The [KI]Grimoire is in the header's Reward, so by rule it proves the quest is over rather than that step 4 is done, and step 4's evidence is null. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is not steps either -- returning to Erlene at Scholar level 5 for Embrava and Kaustra happens after this quest has already ended.
